# Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

A stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars) collects the run's telemetry to the local JSONL
sink whenever the share-telemetry setting is on, and collects nothing when the setting is off
or in a production build.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically collect its run
telemetry, so the run can be evaluated without a manual export step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `resolveEffectiveTelemetryConfig()` (with the settings-driven flag wired in) returns
  `recording: true` with sink `jsonl` when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true and
  `shareTelemetryDev` is true, with **no** `VITE_TELEMETRY_*` env vars set.
- In dev with `shareTelemetryDev === false`, recording is disabled — the game neither collects
  nor uploads (parent AC2). **Plan-time decision:** the setting is the controlling gate for dev
  collection; the env-var escape hatch remains available for production (where it still requires
  consent), and this ordering is asserted by tests.
- In a production build (`PROD === true`) behaviour is unchanged: recording still requires
  `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` plus the consent flag; `shareTelemetryDev` is ignored.
- `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` loads the persisted setting and passes the dev-collection flag
  into config resolution, so a fresh dev session records from run start.
- Unit tests cover the (dev/prod) × (on/off) matrix plus production-consent-unchanged regression,
  and the JSONL sink writes under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` in the happy-dom test env.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/telemetry/config.ts` (and `consent.ts` resolution) with an optional
  `devCollectionEnabled` flag derived from the setting; default `false` so existing callers and
  production envs are unchanged.
- Change the effective recording gate to `DEV ? (setting || existing-resolved-recording) :
  existing-resolved-recording`, keeping the consent path intact — the exact boolean composition is
  pinned by the tests above.
- Update `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` (~line 3872) to `loadSettings()` and pass
  `settings.shareTelemetryDev`.
- Tests in `config.test.ts`, `consent.test.ts` and the PlayScene suite.

**Key Files:**

- `src/telemetry/config.ts`
- `src/telemetry/consent.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/telemetry/config.test.ts`
- `src/telemetry/consent.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (dev gate helper) and F2 (setting field) — collection gating composes with both.

## Deliverables

Dev-gated collection-on-by-default + matrix tests; production behaviour provably unchanged.
data.title: Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode

## Summary
implement.py drive (implement skill) repeatedly tries to 'finish' a child work item that is already in a terminal state (completed), fails every run, and loops forever without the epic advancing. The child should be treated as done, not re-driven.

## Context
Discovered while driving epic AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX (Compile an action video) via /tmp/resilient_drive.sh (discovered-from:AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX). The looping harness itself was an orphan from a dead session and has been killed; this item covers the underlying drive bug.

## Reproduction evidence
/tmp/epic_resilient_drive.log shows 29+ drive runs, every one exiting 1 with:
  'Failed to finish child AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ', sessions_spawned: 0, failed_child: AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ
while wl show AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ reported status=completed, stage=in_review (already terminal). Each run also spent ~600s in phase_drive before failing.

## Expected behaviour
drive must treat children in a terminal stage (completed / in_review) as done, skip them, and continue to the next actionable child rather than failing and looping.

## Acceptance criteria
1. drive on an epic whose failed child is already completed exits without spawning a child session and does not reset the completed child's status.
2. No retry loop: parent_advanced reflects the true state (false only when real blocking work remains).
3. Regression: an epic with genuinely unfinished children still drives them in dependency order as before.

## Goal

As a developer, I need failing-first unit tests that pin the persisted
`controlScheme` contract and the effective-scheme precedence before the
production code exists, so the settings field and resolution helper are driven
by tests (TDD).

## Scope

Add unit tests only — no production changes in this item:

1. `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts` — `controlScheme` in `ai_hell_settings`:
   - the default record exposes `controlScheme: 'asteroids'` when nothing is saved;
   - save → load round-trips both `'asteroids'` and `'fourDirectional'` and leaves the other settings untouched;
   - a legacy record without the field resolves to `'asteroids'` and preserves volume/mute/bindings/telemetry;
   - a non-string value (number, `null`, object) resolves to `'asteroids'`;
   - a value outside the union (e.g. `'orbital'`) resolves to `'asteroids'`.
2. `src/core/playerScheme.test.ts` (new) — the effective-scheme resolution helper:
   - a valid stored setting wins over the ship-config `controlScheme`;
   - an absent/invalid stored setting falls back to the ship-config value;
   - both absent/invalid falls back to the built-in default (`'asteroids'`);
   - the helper never mutates the ship-config object (deep-equal snapshot before/after) and performs no CSV write.

Reference the existing fallback patterns (`resolveBindings`, corrupt-JSON
fallback) in `src/core/settingsStore.ts` for style.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New/updated unit and scene tests cover each of AC1–AC7 (settings round-trip/fallback, resolution helper, SettingsScene control and relabelling, `PlayScene` application) — this item owns its share of parent AC8 and the sibling test item owns the rest.
- Settings-store unit tests assert the default `controlScheme` is `asteroids`, that a saved value is restored, and that legacy, non-string and out-of-union values fall back to `asteroids` — covering the persistence and fallback requirement in full.
- Resolution-helper unit tests assert all three precedence levels (stored setting → ship config `controlScheme` → built-in default) and that the ship config is never mutated.
- Tests fail for the expected reason before items "Persist player control scheme in settings" and "Resolve effective player control scheme" land (red), then pass (green) after them.
- Tests are run through the test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope) — never an ad-hoc runner invocation.

## Key Files

- `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts` — controlScheme round-trip, legacy/corrupt fallback cases.
- `src/core/playerScheme.test.ts` — new spec for the precedence helper.

## Constraints

- Test-only change: no production code in this item.
- Follow the existing vitest style and helpers already used in `settingsStore.test.ts`.
- Use UK English in descriptions and comments.

## Definition of done

- The new tests exist, are wired into the existing suites, and are red for the right reasons.
- `/skill:test` (changed scope) has been run and the red state is recorded in a comment.

## Parent AC coverage

Covers parent AC2 (persistence and fallback, test half), AC3 (precedence, test half)
and AC8 (tests) from "Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player".
